To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the Italian shadow economy is large and growing and that (ii) the tax burden is high, but the tax gap is not.

(a) the shadow economy is a significant share of the Italian economy (about one fifth of GDP), (b) the Italian method to compute the shadow economy is reliable, (c) the shadow economy affects national accounts, (d) the tax burden is an important driver of the shadow economy, (e) the tax burden and the shadow economy go hand-in-hand, and (f) the tax burden has been decreasing over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hidden gaps in fiscal rules and national accounts.
the effects of shadow economy on the national accounts, fiscal policy and fiscal sustainability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
underground activities affect crucial fiscal policy ratios generating “gapses” both in government receipts and in national accounts.
the shadow economy is a relevant phenomenon that should be considered in any analysis on the Italian economy.
the shadow economy is a major source of uncertainty in fiscal policy and that the Italian case is not a happy one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shadow economy is an important issue to consider when assessing the state of the Italian economy and the effectiveness of fiscal policy.
the underground economy affects the fiscal stance of the Italian government, both through the tax burden and through the national accounts.
the Italian fiscal policy is a game of hidden gaps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while underground activities are a major issue for fiscal policy, the impact on fiscal ratios is not necessarily negative.
the shadow economy is not a mere technical issue but it affects the whole fiscal policy process.
the hidden economy is a crucial element in understanding the Italian economy and the policy debate.
